clue.text: Might we thus describe Amundsen's arrival at 12 for a 19?

definitions.text: Might we thus describe Amundsen's arrival at 12
definitions.meaning: Amundsen reached the South Pole (12 across) weeks before Scott
19 across is BARON, and the Labour politician John ... became Baron ...

explanation.surface: A question about how to describe the Norwegian explorer's polar arrival, oddly tied to a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as PRE-SCOTT: Roald Amundsen got to the South Pole in December 1911, about five weeks before Robert Falcon Scott's British party. John Prescott was Labour's Deputy Prime Minister and later took a seat in the Lords as a baron.
explanation.definitionFit: John Prescott, former Deputy Prime Minister, was made a life peer with the title Baron Prescott.

clue.text: Commercial break without purpose

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an AD
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: An advert break that seems to serve no point at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting without direction or aim, as a boat cut loose; figuratively aimless.

clue.text: Vehicle with excellent emperor carrying British cop abroad

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the word for excellent holds the British abbreviation inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A fine emperor in a car, transporting a British policeman overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is written AI, the figure 1 read as the letter I; 'carrying' puts the B inside it to make ABI.
explanation.definitionFit: A carabinero is a member of a Spanish (or Latin American) police or frontier force, so a foreign policeman.

clue.text: Works harnessing power in river succeeded

indicators.note: the river is said to harness the power, so the power letter sits within the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England
P is the physics symbol for power
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A hydroelectric scheme that harnesses a river's power, and it worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harnessing' puts P inside OUSE, then S follows. The English plural is used here rather than the Latin 'opera'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a creative piece, especially a musical composition, so opuses are works of art.

clue.text: Ready to embrace better harlot

indicators.note: the word for ready is wrapped round the other word, as in an embrace

parts.note: set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'
to trump is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Someone poised to hug a person who is superior to them, followed by a harlot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the adjective; it is the verb, as when a card trumps another. 'to embrace' wraps one piece round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet and harlot are both old-fashioned words for a prostitute or promiscuous woman.

clue.text: Blackwood's Batter!

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A cheer for Jermaine Blackwood, the West Indies cricketer, as he bats.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Blackwood' into 'Black wood' to give B + ASH; the possessive 's is just glue. The surface makes Blackwood the batsman and 'Batter' a noun; in the answer it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash is to hit hard repeatedly, the same as to batter.

clue.text: Shape is round, involving a square

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the following word, as if involving it within them
to shape something is to form it anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A geometry instruction: a shape that is round yet somehow includes a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shape' rearranges IS ROUND to DINOSUR, and 'involving' puts A inside it. 'square' is a noun for an old-fashioned person, not the geometric figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is a person with outdated views, just as a square is someone hopelessly conventional.

clue.text: News boss taking fresh drink round sacked dour companion

indicators.note: the drink goes round the word for fresh, enclosing it

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
pert means cheeky, impudent, the same as fresh

indicators.note: sacked here means ransacked, thrown about, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A media chief with a new drink in hand, having fired a gloomy colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the drink about the fresh word, and 'sacked' makes URDO from the gloomy one. CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Murdoch heads News Corporation, the media company that owns many newspapers.

clue.text: Special welcome Yorkshire town cherished

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire, England
pet as an adjective means favourite or cherished

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire town gives a warm, special welcome to a much-loved visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet is the idiom for giving a VIP a ceremonial welcome.

clue.text: We're going to pass on gold rings

indicators.note: the gold symbol surrounds the other piece, ringing it

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to pass on is to die

explanation.surface: A couple leaving their gold rings to someone as they depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' is the verb, surrounding. 'pass on' looks like handing something down; here it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, said by people who are leaving.

clue.text: Victor on one has moved around destroyer

indicators.note: the letters are shifted around into a new order

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A naval tale: Victor, aboard a ship, has steered around a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved around' rearranges V, I and HAS. 'destroyer' suggests a warship, but here it is the god.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism Shiva is the destroyer god within the trinity alongside Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver.

clue.text: Banned brown sauce in fish where seas freeze

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the fish word

parts.note: sole is a flatfish
out means banned, ruled out
HP Sauce is the best-known British brown sauce, a spicy condiment

explanation.surface: A menu ban: no brown sauce on the fish in some frozen place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts both pieces inside the fish. HP Sauce is a popular British brown table sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic sea round the southernmost point of Earth freezes over each winter.

clue.text: Proves smarter than fools at Brasenose?

parts.note: Brasenose is an Oxford college, and OU stands for Oxford University
twits are fools

explanation.surface: Clever students get one over on the idiots at an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: Brasenose is a college of Oxford University, abbreviated OU in its societies' names; the question mark flags that it stands for the whole university.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to beat them by being cleverer, to prove smarter than them.

clue.text: Display struggle for breath over time

indicators.note: the panting word is spread over the time word, covering it from both sides

parts.note: to pant is to struggle for breath
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A display so tiring that viewers gasp for air for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' means the breathless word spans the time word, holding it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public show or spectacle, often a procession in costume.

clue.text: Sweet shot with son in black hat?

parts.note: a go is a shot or attempt

indicators.note: the son letter is put within the black hat pieces

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: A boy in a black top hat having a go at a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside B + TOPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gobstopper is a large, hard, round sweet, a jawbreaker in American English.

clue.text: Board to suggest schedule

definitions.meaning: board means food served at meals
to ... a motion is to put it forward for discussion

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a dining surface for meals, putting forward a proposal, and a list such as a timetable.

clue.text: Conversation in pub about radius in diagram

indicators.note: the conversation goes about the radius letter, enclosing it

parts.note: bar chat is chit-chat in a pub

explanation.surface: Chat in a pub about a circle's radius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside BAR CHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar chart is a graph showing quantities as bars of varying length.

clue.text: Maybe Lion King not shown in Barrow?

indicators.note: the king letter is left out, kept from view

parts.note: a barrow is a small cart
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A cinema in Barrow not screening the film The Lion King.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow-in-Furness is a Cumbrian town, but here a barrow is a cart; 'Maybe' marks the lion as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is one of the big wild felines, an example of the family that includes house moggies.

clue.text: Getting together in Soho: nice to get wasted

indicators.note: getting wasted means getting drunk, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A night out in London's Soho, where it is nice to get drunk with friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get wasted' rearranges SOHO and NICE. Soho is a London nightlife district.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesion is the act or state of sticking or uniting together.

clue.text: Nobleman not producing results in speech

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, matching the spoken form of the answer

parts.note: barren means unproductive, yielding nothing

explanation.surface: A lord whose talks produce nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' says BARREN aloud, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the British peerage.

clue.text: Approach faction in British Left

parts.note: to near is to approach
a side is a faction or party in a dispute

explanation.surface: Making overtures to a group within the British political Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks political but means the left-hand side of a car; Britain drives on the left, so the kerb side is the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The nearside of a vehicle is the side nearest the kerb, which in Britain is its left.

clue.text: See 8
See 26
Atlantic liner docked, located by a satellite

indicators.note: docked means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the Titanic was the liner that sank in the Atlantic

explanation.surface: A transatlantic liner moored, its position fixed by a satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks nautical but means curtailed: TITANIC loses its final C.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the largest moon of Uranus, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Dialogue tense on very right-wing channel

parts.note: talk is dialogue or conversation
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Talk with a tense tone on a highly right-wing broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: TalkTV was a British TV channel owned by Murdoch's News UK, launched in 2022 with Piers Morgan as a host.
explanation.definitionFit: TalkTV was a British broadcaster known for opinionated conservative presenters.

clue.text: Required Scots hooligan to cross rising river

indicators.note: the hooligan's word straddles the river word, taking it inside

parts.note: ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan or thug

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: A Scottish thug had to wade across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the river upwards as EED, since this is a down clue, and 'to cross' sets it inside the hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required both mean necessary, wanted as essential.

clue.text: Tries to stop serious practice session

indicators.note: the trying word plugs the gap within the serious word, as a stopper does

parts.note: real means serious, genuine
a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: An attempt to halt a session that is no longer playful but serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' plugs one piece into the other. 'Tries' looks like attempts; here it is the legal sense of hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a run-through before a performance, practising it.

clue.text: Final word not entirely correct

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, its last letter missing

parts.note: to amend is to correct

explanation.surface: A last word that is not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final D of AMEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of a prayer or hymn, the last thing uttered.

clue.text: Sacked tabloid editor supports newspaper, investing millions

parts.note: piers are supports, as for a bridge
an organ is a newspaper or periodical voicing a group's views

explanation.surface: A fired tabloid editor props up a paper by pouring in millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' signals M added to ORGAN as money is put into it. Piers Morgan was sacked as editor of the Daily Mirror in 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: Piers Morgan edited the News of the World and Daily Mirror, losing the latter job over faked photographs.

clue.text: Be at one match

definitions.meaning: to be at one is to be in harmony, to concur
two things that match correspond with each other

explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be at one; figures or accounts that tally are said to correspond.

clue.text: Improving new image recurring in Bond, initially discarded

indicators.note: the new pieces are placed inside what is left of Bond
the opening letter of the word is thrown away

parts.note: Bond is taken as written before its first letter goes
a theme is a recurring image or motif

explanation.surface: A fresh, repeated image in a James Bond film, its opening scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially discarded' leaves OND, and 'in' sets the new pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: On the mend is an idiom for recovering from illness, getting better.
